findings.issue: Regression introduced by the M1 fix. In the documentary edition the English Tisgav and Veyeetayu rubrics are English sentences with one embedded Hebrew word. The new rule now treats that word as a separate top-level direction run and forces line breaks around it. p. 9 now reads 'In Frankfurt a. M. and many congre-gations' / 'תשגב' / 'is not said.' and p. 10 reads 'In Fuerth and other communities the reader now sings:' / 'ויאתיו' / 'but in Frankfurt a. M., Metz and many communities this prayer is omitted.' The pre-fix documentary render (final-documentary-11/12.png, viewed only to compare) set both sentences inline. This contradicts the resolution note ('inline foreign phrases unchanged'), and it creates in the documentary view the same kind of broken reading order that M1 fixed in the expanded view. No words are lost.
findings.required_change: Narrow the break rule. Separate runs only at language-block boundaries: for example, between child elements that carry different xml:lang (the expanded case, a de-Hebr block followed by an English block). Do not break around an inline foreign-language segment that sits inside running text of the note's main language (a he span with text in the note's language on both sides). Add a negative regression test using an EN instruction note with an embedded he word, as in the documentary Tisgav/Veyeetayu notes, that asserts no forced break. Keep the existing positive expanded test. Re-render documentary-final-review.pdf, refresh accepted-documentary-11/12 and the manifest hashes, and re-run final-pdf-log-evidence for the new PDF. The expanded output should not change.
